analysis:
The PR changes only docs/architecture/inference.md. The file_changes patch shows a date bump (2026-10-22 to 2026-10-23), a GLM video-handling description (frame timing now i / nominalFrameRate, variable-frame-rate tracks indexed instead of refused), and a deleted clause saying VFR video returns 400. Further head ranges (876-880, 1717-1726) are outside the supplied excerpts. Both units are docs-only, with no executable code, config, or authorization changes, so I found no security regression.

The supplied units are the base Flint/Bonsai tail (lines 2366-2597) and the head start (lines 1-415, the Nemotron Super text). Neither contains the changed GLM video lines, so the substance of the GLM change could only be read from the patch excerpt.

Security-relevant observation: if the underlying code really stopped refusing variable-frame-rate video, that widens the media-decoding surface (TB-003/TB-007, T-050 plaintext video handling; T-029 resource consumption). The docs still cite the 512 MiB decoded-frame cap (maximumDecodedBytes) and the 28,532 visual-token prepared-pixel cap. I cannot verify from the supplied evidence that these bounds hold for VFR tracks (for example, frame counts derived from nominalFrameRate versus actual samples). Any code change is outside this batch. I did not verify that the documentation matches the implementation.

The Nemotron and prefix-cache text (HMAC lookup tags, cache scope partitioning, no scope means cold with no publishing) is consistent with T-041's posture. It is unchanged by this PR and I did not examine it for pre-existing issues.

A deeper pass should check whether the provider source for GLM video decoding (GLM5NextProcessor.decodeAsset) changed in the same PR and still enforces its bounds for VFR input.
